problem:
A company collected data on the sale price (in thousands of dollars) of a particular used car model and the car's age (in years). This data is shown below.

| Age $(x)$ | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** | **$7$** | **$8$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Price $(y)$ | $12$ | $10$ | $8.5$ | $7$ | $6.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the sale price of a model that is $10$ years old, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}38 & -6 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}44 \\ 250\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
